what_happened: Recovered the full text of the cut app:presheaf-dictionary Reflection clause and def:behavior-presheaf from the paper repo's git history (commit b64b1ca0^, the commit before 'task 149: cut category-theory material'), and then compiled the entire clause end-to-end as a scratch probe on the first iteration after one tactic substitution. ref laws, section reflection, naturality, involution and the Equiv all type-check with zero sorries and measure [propext, Quot.sound].

The converse frame this task must consume (FrameOver.rev / TaskFrame.rev) is sited in FormalSystem/OpenLanguage/OpenReversal.lean, which is ABOVE the Semantics layer. A compiled probe proved that importing it into the Presheaf cluster trips the cluster's assert_not_exists FormalSystem.ProofSystem.Axiom guard through a ten-link chain (OpenReversal -> OpenValidity -> OpenTruth -> OpenClasses -> PlusPasting -> PlusValidity -> Semantics.Validity -> ValidityLayer -> FrameClassValidity -> ProofSystem.Axioms). Reuse therefore requires promoting the frame-level reversal block down into Semantics/, which widens file_scope beyond the single declared Reflection.lean.

Two pointers in the task description are stale. The swapUS/swapMinus families it names as 'still under review in task 608' do not exist anywhere in the tree and task 608 is absent from state.json. And the paper anchor instruction to read the Reflection clauses as COMMENTED OUT text in possible_worlds.tex cannot be followed: a later commit ('task 130 phase 1: retire pre-existing source comments and dead commented-out blocks') deleted the commented block, leaving only a one-sentence preview at line 1921. The text was recovered from git history instead.

The research report's Phase A (promote FrameOver.rev/TaskFrame.rev from OpenLanguage/OpenReversal.lean down into Semantics/TaskFrame.lean, widening file_scope and raising a user_decision) is already done: task 796 phase 2 (commit bf33d8e71) landed the ConverseFrame section in Semantics/TaskFrame.lean and Semantics/Reversal.lean. Re-derived at plan time by compiling the saved probe with its simulated block stripped against the current tree: exit 0, zero sorries, all five results measure [propext, Quot.sound], assert_not_exists guard passes. The plan therefore needs no scope widening and no user_decision; the clause consumes the sited converse frame directly.
Phase 1 start: saved probe reflection-clause-probe.lean already compiles the full clause against the landed ConverseFrame section; no sentinel at .plan-revised.json, plan text taken as-is.

Phase 1 commit was blocked by the pre-commit typst-sync-check Check 2 gate: adding a new .lean file moves formalsystem-file-count/line-count in typst/generated/status.typ. Plan did not list status.typ regeneration as a per-phase step. Resolved by running scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix after the green build and staging typst/generated/status.typ with each phase commit (same pattern as the sibling Duration module's commits). The accompanying warning that FormalSystem.lean has 710 imports vs 711 files is deferred to Phase 3, where the root import is added together with the aggregator import.

scripts/check-paper-definitions.sh exits 1 with 9 drifted PINNED definitions (def:task-relation etc.: the external paper changed enumerate options, e.g. [wide=0pt,...] -> [named]). Pre-existing and independent of this task: the identical failure reproduces against the HEAD record (--record <git show HEAD:...>), and this task edits only the free text of two DANGLING rows, pinning nothing. The plan's 'exits 0' criterion for this gate therefore cannot be met by this task; the part under its control (cut anchors stay DANGLING, no pin attempted) holds. Re-pinning the drifted definitions is a separate task on the paper-record front.
